learning.title: Verify shared-service consumers before retiring an idle workspace
learning.trigger: An idle workspace is being closed and its checkout is being archived or removed.
learning.mistake: Assumed closing the workspace released every consumer of its checkout, then removed the checkout or stopped shared services to complete cleanup.
learning.rule: Use this as a procedural safety rule, not as a shipped retirement utility: before normal removal, create and restore an archive in a separate temporary verification location, then run ownership-scoped git worktree, /proc cwd/fd, and container mount/consumer inspections. If any shared or uncertain consumer remains, preserve the checkout; never force-delete it or kill, restart, or reconfigure the shared service.

verification.requirement: Verify archive and restore bytes, hashes, modes, symlinks, and bundle contents, then perform fresh cwd, entrypoint, and mount-consumer checks before removal. Record the evidence and retention condition; never overwrite the live checkout during archive/restore verification.

learning.boundary: Workspace-session state is not sufficient proof that shared service consumers are gone. Preserve the checkout and continue unrelated work when consumer ownership cannot be safely retired.
